name: GitSpace
tagline: A familiar Git desktop workflow, running as one shared Uno app
summary: GitSpace is an independent, MIT-licensed Git client with a GitHub Desktop-style interface, built in C# and Uno Platform. Review changes in unified or split diffs, stage individual lines, commit, browse history, manage branches and sync remotes. On desktop it drives your installed Git; in the browser, the same compiled Uno UI runs against a bundled Git worker that writes real repositories to IndexedDB.

heroStats.label: real Git backends: system Git and browser worker

highlights.title: Same app on desktop and web
highlights.text: The browser build is the actual compiled Uno application, sharing the workbench and custom controls with the Win32, macOS and X11 desktop hosts.

highlights.title: Real Git in the browser
highlights.text: A bundled isomorphic-git worker writes genuine objects, refs and index to IndexedDB via LightningFS, off the UI thread. No in-memory simulation.

highlights.title: Skia-rendered diff viewer
highlights.text: Unified and split diffs with line gutters, intraline highlights, search, whitespace-ignore and text zoom, drawn viewport-only through SKCanvasElement.

highlights.title: Line and hunk staging
highlights.text: Select exact lines or hunks in Unstaged/Staged modes, update the index safely and make staged-only commits.

highlights.title: Graphical conflict resolver
highlights.text: On desktop, resolve conflicts in a current/incoming/result editor with stale-content guards and an explicit Mark resolved step.

highlights.title: GitHub pull requests
highlights.text: List the first 100 open pull requests, create a new one, or open the repository or PR in the browser using a session-only token.

highlights.title: Safety by design
highlights.text: No force push, hooks disabled for GitSpace commands, confirmations for destructive actions and no simulated success behind unsupported menus.

highlights.title: Bounded, measurable limits
highlights.text: Myers diff with an explicit work budget, 2 MiB preview limit, 16 MiB output caps and an LRU text-blob cache keep work predictable.

items: Open, initialize and HTTPS-clone repositories; refresh and add HTTPS remotes
Real, editable tutorial repository with four commits opens on first launch
Recent repositories and persisted non-secret preferences
Browser repositories exported as ZIP (.git + working files, up to 64 MiB)
Changed-file list with inclusion checkboxes, stage and unstage
Unified and split diffs with line numbers and intraline split highlights
Diff search, whitespace-ignore view, copy and text zoom
Exact line/hunk selection in Unstaged and Staged review modes
Explicit unsupported preview for binary and image files
Bounded UTF-8 file editor with new files and an external-change check before saving
Tracked-file discard with confirmation; untracked files are never deleted by Discard
Commit composer with required summary, optional description and author identity
Selected-file commits and confirmed amend of the latest commit
Preserves BOMs and mixed newline conventions in unchanged content
Paged history in 200-commit pages up to 2,000 commits, with filter
Author, date, message and per-commit file changes with parent comparison
Create, switch and rename branches; safe merged-branch deletion
Lightweight tags
Fetch, fast-forward pull and non-force push
Desktop merge, rebase, revert and cherry-pick with continue/abort
Desktop current/incoming/result conflict editor with explicit Mark resolved
Tracked/untracked stash, apply without dropping and confirmed drop on desktop
Explicit, user-configured trusted CORS proxy for browser clone/fetch/push
List the first 100 open pull requests
Create a pull request from the app
Open the repository or a pull request in the browser
Session-only token authentication; tokens never persisted
Compact menu bar with repository, branch and sync tiles
Changes and History tabs with a resizable sidebar
Light and dark appearances
Keyboard shortcuts, explicit errors and busy state
Embedded Source Code Pro font for consistent monospace diff metrics

codeSamples.title: Use the Git backend without Uno
Run the desktop app from source
codeSamples.code:
git clone https://github.com/wieslawsoltes/GitSpace.git
cd GitSpace
dotnet run --project src/GitSpace.App -f net10.0-desktop \
  -p:GitSpaceTargetFrameworks=net10.0-desktop

playground.intro: Open the live WebAssembly build and work in a real, persisted tutorial repository stored in your browser.

tour.title: Review the tutorial changes
tour.text: The tutorial repository opens on first launch with uncommitted changes. Select files in the Changes tab and inspect their diffs.

tour.title: Switch diff views
tour.text: Toggle between unified and split diffs, search within the diff, and zoom the text.

tour.title: Stage lines and commit
tour.text: Click, Shift-click or Ctrl-click changed lines to stage a selection, write a summary in the commit composer and commit to real Git history.

tour.title: Browse history and branch
tour.text: Open the History tab to see per-commit file changes, then create and switch to a new branch.

tour.title: Change appearance and identity
tour.text: Toggle light/dark appearance and set your Git author name and email in Preferences; reload to see everything persist.

tour.title: Take your work with you
tour.text: Use File → Export repository ZIP to download the .git folder and working files.

architecture.name: Contracts and algorithms
architecture.text: Portable repository contracts, validation and a bounded Myers diff with no UI or Skia dependency.

architecture.name: Backends
architecture.text: Interchangeable IGitBackend implementations for installed Git and a browser worker, plus a GitHub REST client.

architecture.name: Rendering
architecture.text: Viewport-only Skia diff renderer with cached paints, fonts and split alignment.

architecture.name: Controls
architecture.text: Custom Uno controls that communicate through events and never touch repositories or the network.

architecture.name: Workbench
architecture.text: Embeddable client workspace composed from the controls, driven by an injected platform and backend.

boundaries: 0.1.0 development preview, not complete or pixel-qualified GitHub Desktop parity
Browser merge and pull are fast-forward only; rebase, revert, cherry-pick and conflict editor are desktop only
Browser clone/fetch/push to GitHub usually needs a CORS proxy you configure and trust
Browser storage can be evicted; export a ZIP or push to preserve important work
No OAuth/account switching, GitHub Enterprise, LFS/submodule/worktree UI or interactive rebase
